title: Understanding Cristian Volpato Salary: How to Convert Hourly to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert hourly rates to annual salary using the 38-hour week, including casual loading and super. Cristian Volpato salary example included.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then multiply by 52. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, annual pay is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,253.44.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave entitlements. It is calculated as base rate × 1.25. For example, the National Minimum Wage casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. When using our timesheet tool, check the casual loading box to add it automatically; never enter a rate that already includes loading.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in my hourly rate or paid on top?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee is 12% of your gross pay, up to the maximum contribution base ($270,830 for 2026–27). It does not reduce your take-home pay; your employer adds it separately. For example, on a $26.44 hourly rate, super is an extra $3.17 per hour, but you only see that in your super account.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Hourly to Annual Pay

Whether you're calculating **Cristian Volpato salary** or your own, the method is the same. Annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by the hours you work each week, multiplied by 52 weeks. For a standard full‑time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula is:

**Hourly rate × 38 × 52 = annual gross pay**

This assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates or allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It gives you a baseline figure before tax and super.

### Example with the National Minimum Wage

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Commission is $26.44 per hour for a 38‑hour week ($1,004.90 per week). Using the formula:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,253.44 per year

This is the minimum annual pay for an adult employee not covered by an award or agreement. Most employees are covered by an award, which may have higher rates.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) for each award. Award minimum wages increased by 4.75% from 1 July 2026. Always check the correct award for your industry. The National Minimum Wage applies only to award/agreement‑free employees. For award‑covered employees, the award rate is the minimum.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid sick leave or annual leave. The casual National Minimum Wage is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour.

When using [the timesheet](/), tick the casual loading checkbox to add the 25% automatically. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the tool adds it for you.

## Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross pay. It does not reduce your take‑home pay. The maximum earnings base for super is $270,830 per year (2026–27). For a full‑time worker on the National Minimum Wage, annual super is $52,253.44 × 12% = $6,270.41.

## Tax and Take‑Home Pay

Your take‑home pay depends on tax withheld. The 2026–27 resident tax rates are:

- Nil up to $18,200
- 15% from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with reduction thresholds for low income earners). Use the Australian Taxation Office's gross pay estimator to estimate net pay.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. Simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. For the National Minimum Wage: $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80 per fortnight before tax.

## Average Weekly Earnings

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (May 2026), full‑time adult ordinary time earnings average $2,083.70 per week. All employees (including part‑time) average $1,579.20 per week. These figures help benchmark your salary.

### Using the Timesheet Tool

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and toggle casual loading. It calculates annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay, plus estimated tax and super. Remember: super is paid on top, and the tool shows it separately.

### Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more details, see our [reference tables](/data) and [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) pages.
